macro_context.market_sentiment: Mixed and cautious: S&P 500 futures +0.5% on May 5 after a risk-off session on May 4 (Dow -1.13%, S&P -0.41%, Nasdaq -0.19%) driven by escalating U.S.-Iran conflict. May 1 saw record Nasdaq and S&P closes, so the broader trend year-to-date remains bullish but fragile.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29 (8-4 vote, most dissents since 1992). Median forecast remains one cut in 2026, pushed later due to elevated inflation partly from Middle East oil price spike. Powell stepping down as chair but remaining on the Board; markets pricing near-zero probability of a 2026 cut.
macro_context.geopolitical: U.S.-Iran conflict in month three with no resolution; UAE intercepted Iranian missiles May 4, sending crude oil above $104 (WTI). Strait of Hormuz traffic near standstill. Chinese semiconductor overcapacity and U.S. export controls add supply chain pressure for chip companies. Tariff uncertainty and midterm elections loom.

Upgrades: DA Davidson raised to Buy from Neutral, PT $375; Stifel raised PT to $320. Net consensus remains Buy (34 analysts) with average PT ~$307 (range $240-$400). Source: Benzinga, MarketBeat, TipRanks

web_context.competitor_activity: NVIDIA holds 75-80% of AI accelerator market and remains Wall Street's highest-conviction AI play; analysts project 30-40% NVDA upside. Intel reported Q1 2026 beat and guidance raise on April 23, with Intel stock up 164% YTD — far outpacing AMD's run. On May 4, AMD fell -5.27% while Intel was -2% and NVDA -1%, signaling a selective AI chip trade divergence against AMD. AMD's server upside is constrained by TSMC foundry capacity limits, unlike NVDA which has prioritized supply. The biggest competitive threat to NVDA is actually hyperscaler custom silicon (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium), not AMD. Source: 24/7wallst.com, ibtimes.com

Data center revenue consensus $5.56B (+51.5% YoY).
